Resolves #20481

🌿 A slow runner can no longer fail a resize that was visibly live.

`HeaderMenuInteractionNL`'s motion receipt now asserts what only it can show: the header's width rises in at least two steps under the held pointer, never one jump at the drop. It no longer requires `> box.width + 40` to land inside the fixed 1800 ms window. That target stays asserted without a clock, by the held-pointer DOM poll and the post-drop component poll. The window's placement (#20455) and length are unchanged.

Evidence: L2 (the CI receipt that failed, re-checked against the new predicate; local off-socket e2e-engine runs) → L2 required (a CI-only flake whose cause is in the attached receipt). Residual: none.

## AC Evidence

| AC | Evidence |
|---|---|
| AC-1 | `HeaderMenuInteractionNL.spec.mjs:356–360`: `rises >= 2` over the sampled widths, and `max > box.width` |
| AC-2 | The predicate passes the run-42282441953 receipt (16 rises; the old check fails it). It fails a synthetic flat-then-jump receipt (1 rise) and a flat one (0), and passes live growth with a 1 px snap at the drop |
| AC-3 | `durationMs: 1800` and both `> box.width + 40` polls are untouched |
| AC-4 | Local, off-socket tier with no Brain checkout: the full spec, 15 of 15 (5 tests × `--repeat-each=3`) |

## Deltas from ticket

- The ticket first listed "none decreasing, last above the start". I dropped both before implementing (the ticket body records why): a one-pixel snap at the drop would trip them without saying anything about live resize. The synthetic snap case above pins that.

## Test Evidence

- Root cause, from the failing shard's trace attachment (`header-resize-motion`): the width grew live from 150 to 190 px by 1738 ms, with 26 samples where a 32 ms interval gives about 56 (a contended runner). The strict `> 190` check failed as the window closed.
- Local: `env -u NEO_MCP_REMOTE_TOKEN -u NEO_AGENTOS_RUNTIME_ROOT NEO_NL_PORT=<free> npx playwright test -c test/playwright/playwright.config.e2e.mjs test/playwright/e2e/grid/HeaderMenuInteractionNL.spec.mjs --repeat-each=3` gave 15 passed, exit 0.

## Post-Merge Validation

- [ ] The next e2e-engine runs carrying this spec show no `:356` motion failure.
